findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the deterministic ranking/tie-break used to select the kept candidates when qualifiers exceed the per-side/8-case cap.
evidence: 'Per criterion at most 8 cases, targeting 4 expect: finding and 4 expect: pass'
'Two consecutive real runs over the committed corpus emit byte-identical output'
ABSENCE: no tie-break/ranking (e.g. by decision_margin, then row id) is stated for choosing among surplus candidates
findings.finding: When a criterion yields more qualifying candidates than the 8-case cap (or more than 4 per side), the plan states no ordering/selection rule for which candidates are kept, yet an AC requires byte-identical output across runs.
findings.location: 'Emitted shape and balance guarantee' ('at most 8 cases, targeting 4 finding and 4 pass'); Acceptance Criteria (diff -r determinism)
scenarios: A high-traffic criterion has 30 fire candidates; without a pinned deterministic ordering, dict/set iteration order can pick a different 4, breaking the diff -r determinism AC.
findings.suggested_fix: Rank kept candidates by descending abs(decision_margin) then by row id, and state that ordering explicitly.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the per-ticket escaped-defect signal is attributed to a specific criterion before it seeds that criterion's expect:finding case (e.g. restrict to the criterion(s) named on the culprit bug, or drop escaped-defect as a per-criterion fire source).
evidence: Plan: 'a ticket that passed review then took a plan_defect close or an inbound caused_by link ... is a must-fire candidate' — no criterion attribution named
labels.escaped_defect(ticket_state) is keyed on the TICKET (close_class / inbound_deps), returning a single bool with no per-criterion breakdown
Scope emits 'at most 8 cases' PER CRITERION, so the escaped-defect signal must be joined to a criterion, but the plan states no join key
findings.finding: The escaped-defect FIRE signal produces a per-criterion `expect: finding` case, but an escaped defect (plan_defect close / inbound caused_by) is a per-TICKET fact with no attribution to the specific criterion C the miner is emitting for. A ticket whose escaped defect belongs to criterion X can thus seed a must-fire case under an unrelated criterion Y, mislabeling the fixture.
findings.location: Approach → Signals → 'Escaped defect, positive use only'; escaped_defect at labels.py:62-73
scenarios: A ticket escapes a defect that belonged to G3 (decomposition); the miner attaches an expect:finding case to G6 because G6 also lacked a spec and the ticket passed review
The mined G6 fixture then asserts G6 must fire on a plan whose only defect was a G3 concern, making the oracle wrong

findings.checklist_item: Define the join that lets a single finding hold BOTH reproduction consensus (equal-fingerprint pair) AND resolved_by_author (differing-material churn pair) — name the unit (e.g. norm_id over the ticket's full review sequence) and confirm a non-empty population can satisfy all four blocking conjuncts.
evidence: Plan: BLOCKING requires 'reproduction consensus, author-response corroboration, abs(decision_margin) ... and the vintage gate'
labels.py:15-16 docstring: 'Reviews of *differing* material instead measure real churn: which findings persisted vs. were resolved (classify_finding_survival)'
Reproduction consensus signal: 'consistently across two or more reviews with equal material_fingerprint'

The plan does not state the join unit (norm_id across a ticket's full review chain? a specific pair?) linking the equal-fingerprint consensus observation to the differing-material resolved_by_author observation
findings.finding: The BLOCKING conjunction requires, for the same finding, BOTH reproduction consensus (≥2 reviews with EQUAL material_fingerprint) AND author-response corroboration (finding_survival == resolved_by_author). But labels.classify_finding_survival derives resolved_by_author from a consecutive review pair over DIFFERING material (churn), whereas reproduction consensus is defined over an EQUAL-fingerprint pair. The plan never specifies how one finding is joined across these two structurally different pair relationships, leaving the load-bearing blocking definition mechanically incomplete.
findings.location: Approach → 'Tiered admission bar' (four-way conjunction); labels.py:158-171 vs. Reproduction-consensus signal
scenarios: A finding that reproduced across identical material but was never followed by a material-changing review that dropped it can never satisfy both conjuncts — no FIRE candidate ever reaches BLOCKING, silently collapsing the tier to ADVISORY
Or the two signals are joined by norm_id across the whole review chain in a way the plan leaves unspecified, so implementers guess and the tier assignment becomes non-reproducible

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the full emitted-spec schema the miner writes — `prompt` id, `epochs`, the `at_least(k)` `gate` (with k<=epochs), coverage threshold, the deterministic gating scorer(s), and the `gold_set` entry `input`/`label` vocabulary — so validate_eval_spec(strict=True) provably returns zero errors.
evidence: Plan defines the emitted shape only as: 'Per criterion at most 8 cases, targeting 4 expect: finding and 4 expect: pass, plus a non-empty gold_set (eval.py:265-267)'.
AC#8: 'Every emitted spec returns zero errors from validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)'.

eval.py:288-300 requires a `prompt` id, `epochs` (explicit int >= 1), and a parseable `at_least(k)` gate with k <= epochs; the validator docstring (275-284) additionally requires a coverage threshold, >=1 scorer, and >=1 DETERMINISTIC gating scorer.
eval.py:269-271: each gold_set entry must have both a truthy `input` and a truthy `label`; the plan never states what `label` values the mined gold_set carries.
The emitting protocol (how the miner populates prompt/epochs/gate/coverage/scorers/gold-labels) is not co-located with the schema-completeness requirement it must satisfy — a T8 (a)/(b) gap.
findings.finding: The emitted eval-spec schema's required-field vocabulary is left undefined, yet the plan asserts every emitted file passes validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True) with zero errors.
findings.location: Approach → 'Emitted shape and balance guarantee'; Acceptance Criteria bullet 8
scenarios: The miner emits cases + a gold_set but omits epochs/gate/coverage/scorers, so validate_eval_spec(strict=True) returns non-empty errors and AC#8 fails.
Emitted gold_set entries carry an `input` but no `label` (or a label whose vocabulary the harness does not accept), tripping eval.py:270-271.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Emitted spec fields' subsection enumerating every field validate_eval_spec(strict=True) requires (prompt, epochs, gate, coverage/at_least, deterministic scorer name from eval_scorers, and gold_set entry {input,label} with its allowed label values), and derive each field's value from the mined data.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Qualify the bare 'manifest.py:139-185' and 'sidecar.py:344-367' citations with their real package path (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/), distinguishing them from the plan_replay/ modules the miner consumes.
evidence: Scope: 'consuming plan_replay/corpus.py and plan_replay/labels.py' — but list of src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/ has no sidecar.py or manifest.py
registry_version lives at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:139-185 (the regver hash)
_decision_margin lives at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:344-360, not plan_replay/
docs/adr/0053 & 0064 confirm manifest.py == plan_review/manifest.py
findings.finding: Two load-bearing code citations name bare files ('manifest.py:139-185', 'sidecar.py:344-367') that do NOT exist under the plan_replay/ package the Scope names as the consumed source; the symbols (registry_version/regver, _decision_margin) actually live in the sibling src/rebar/llm/plan_review/ package.
findings.location: Approach → 'Vintage gate' and 'Tiered admission bar'; Context paragraph ('regver (manifest.py:139-185)')
scenarios: An implementer resolves 'sidecar.py' to a non-existent plan_replay/sidecar.py and cannot import _decision_margin
A reviewer of a later pass cannot locate the cited line ranges
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'plan_review/manifest.py:139-185' and 'plan_review/sidecar.py:344-360' so the citations disambiguate from the plan_replay/ package.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the sibling admission-runner component that emits 'unreliable-criterion: <id>' tickets — cite it as a prerequisite (rebar:<C> / depends_on) or state explicitly that the convention is defined by this plan's out-of-scope sibling and only the read side is exercised here.
evidence: search for 'unreliable-criterion' across the repo returns (no matches)

Plan: 'recorded by that child's unreliable-criterion: breaker rather than vanishing' and 'A criterion with an open unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id> ticket is skipped' — with no rebar:<C> citation or depends_on for the sibling that emits it
findings.finding: The plan keys behavior on an 'unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>' ticket-listing convention and a 'sibling admission runner'/'sibling loop' that exist nowhere in the codebase and are cited by no depends_on / prerequisite token, leaving the producer of those tickets and the ownership boundary unenumerated.
findings.location: Approach → 'Output lifecycle and skip list' and 'Emitted shape and balance guarantee'; AC #8
scenarios: The skip-list read finds no such tickets because the sibling that mints them is unbuilt/unlinked, so 'skipped-unbalanced' criteria are never actually skipped in practice

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete working-directory path the miner writes to and the sibling admission runner reads from.
evidence: 'An offline miner emitting CANDIDATE fixture specs to a working directory for the sibling admission runner.'
'Each run writes a fresh temporary tree and atomically replaces the working directory' — no concrete path given
ABSENCE: no Scope/Approach line names where under the repo (or .rebar/) the working directory lives
findings.finding: The 'working directory' the miner atomically replaces and emits into is referenced repeatedly but its path/location is never stated, leaving an executing agent without the write target.
findings.location: Approach ('emitting CANDIDATE fixture specs to a working directory'); 'Output lifecycle and skip list' ('atomically replaces the working directory')
scenarios: An agent implements the miner but cannot know whether output goes to .rebar/evals/candidates/, a tmp path, or elsewhere; the sibling runner then reads a different location.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive or sanity-check MIN_MARGIN against the corpus flip-rate (e.g. a fixture measuring how many block-threshold findings survive the observed noise) rather than asserting 0.15.
evidence: 'abs(decision_margin) at or above the constant MIN_MARGIN = 0.15'
'The margin constant drops findings close enough to block_threshold that a small perturbation flips them'
'551 consecutive review pairs ... flipped verdict 208 times' — noise data present but not used to derive 0.15
ANTI-FP check: the integration test runs over the corpus but does not derive/validate the 0.15 value
findings.finding: MIN_MARGIN = 0.15 is asserted as a threshold, not derived from data, and no step in the plan calibrates or measures it against the corpus even though the corpus records the reviewer-noise it is meant to guard against.
scenarios: 0.15 is too low and flaky findings still reach BLOCKING, or too high and legitimate must-fire candidates never qualify — with no measurement to know which.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the vintage gate resolves the prompt's last-change commit when origin/main is absent (e.g. fall back to the current branch's merge-base or a configured base ref), or make the absent-ref case an explicit surfaced error rather than a silent all-skip.
evidence: Plan quote: 'A review is eligible for criterion C only when review_event_ts postdates the last origin/main commit touching C's resolved prompt file.'
Plan quote: 'A criterion whose resolved file has no committed history ... FAILS the gate and is skipped, since no review can postdate a commit that does not exist.'

Matrix cell 'Project location and access: server outside the checkout, no unrestricted-local-filesystem assumption' and 'Platform and venue: CI under any provider' — a shallow/single-branch CI fetch or a deployment outside a full checkout may have no origin/main ref.
findings.finding: The vintage gate resolves eligibility against 'the last origin/main commit touching C's resolved prompt file', hardwiring the remote-tracking ref origin/main; in a shape where that ref is absent, every criterion resolves to 'no committed history' and is skipped, so the miner silently emits nothing.
findings.location: Approach → Vintage gate: 'postdates the last origin/main commit touching C's resolved prompt file'
scenarios: remote MCP server / server-outside-the-checkout deployment where the repo has no 'origin' remote or no origin/main ref: the git lookup for the last origin/main commit returns nothing, so EVERY resolved prompt file is treated as having no committed history, the vintage gate FAILS for all criteria, and the miner produces an empty candidate set — a silent no-op the operator sees as 'no fixtures mined' with no error.
CI venue that fetches only the current branch under a different remote name (not 'origin'): same empty-output no-op.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the vintage baseline from a configurable base ref (defaulting to origin/main but falling back to HEAD's history for the prompt file when no remote ref exists), and treat a wholly-unresolvable baseline as a surfaced diagnostic rather than a silent skip of every criterion.
